codeReview.summary: The commit introduces a clean, defensive InterpreterPool service that centralizes Daytona interpreter construction and safe shutdown. It correctly moves interpreter instantiation out of chat_runtime.py, avoids import-time side effects by keeping Daytona imports local to acquire(), and provides robust exception swallowing in release(). The accompanying unit tests cover the primary success and failure paths. No runtime bugs were found, though the commit leaves the new release() method unwired in chat_runtime.py (that wiring happens in the following commit 6e5b1e84).

issues.description: InterpreterPool is a factory/lifecycle helper, not a true pool (no instance reuse, capacity limits, or queueing). The name is semantically misleading; a more precise name like InterpreterLifecycle would reduce confusion.

In this commit, build_chat_agent_context only calls pool.acquire() and never calls pool.release(). The release() method exists but is dead code in the production path within this commit. The commit message claims 'Wire into chat_runtime.py' but only acquire is wired. The subsequent commit 6e5b1e84 completes the wiring via _ManagedAgentContext.
Missing test coverage for the generic 'except Exception' fallback in InterpreterPool.acquire. Only ImportError and DaytonaConfigError are tested.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The service is named InterpreterPool but does not implement pooling semantics (no reuse, no capacity). Future workers may assume it behaves like a connection pool. Either renaming to InterpreterLifecycle or adding a docstring clarifying 'factory-style pool' would help.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/fleet_rlm/api/runtime_services/interpreter_pool.py:13 — class InterpreterPool docstring says 'Owns Daytona interpreter acquire/release lifecycle' but never mentions reuse or capacity.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Commit 6ec20856 creates InterpreterPool.release() but does not wire it into chat_runtime.py. The actual release wiring happens in the next commit (6e5b1e84). When reviewing multi-commit features, check branch head to verify the full lifecycle is connected.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: git log shows 6e5b1e84 'refactor: delegate interpreter lifecycle to InterpreterPool in chat_runtime' immediately after 6ec20856. diff of 6ec20856 shows chat_runtime.py only calls pool.acquire().

summary: The create-interpreter-pool commit is a solid, defensive refactor. It extracts interpreter construction into a dedicated service with proper error handling and unit tests. The only gaps are semantic naming (not a true pool) and the fact that release() is defined but not yet wired into the chat runtime within this single commit. No blocking issues.
